# Agentic Guardians

> Agentic Guardians is the runtime trust layer for AI agents. It scores your agent's behaviour before every action runs. It doesn't read prompts. It can't be persuaded. Every block is signed (Ed25519). Anyone can verify it. AI trust you can prove.

The core question: **Do you know what your agent is doing right now?** And does it do what it's told, and only that? Agentic Guardians is built to answer both. It learns each agent's normal action sequences, scores every next action before it runs, and stops deviations before they execute, whether they come from prompt injection, logic drift or hallucination. It watches actions, not words, so it sits outside the language layer that attacks target. It is built for SMEs: lightweight enough to adopt without a large security team, robust enough for regulated workflows. Stage: private beta.

## What it is

- The runtime trust layer for AI agents: behavioural enforcement before execution.
- Input: agent actions (file reads, API calls, shell commands, database queries). Not prompts, not tokens.
- Engine: a statistical behavioural model of each agent's normal action sequences. No language model in the decision path. No rules to write.
- Runs on CPU. No GPU needed. Stays local. No cloud round-trip.
- Outcome on each action: allow, pause for human review, or block, before the action runs.
- Proof: every block is signed (Ed25519). Anyone can verify it. Each block produces a Detection Certificate, a record that supports audits, human review and compliance evidence.
- Designed to align with NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 27001 and GDPR.

## The problem

- Your AI agent is already out there. Do you know what it's doing right now?
- Agents drift. They make things up. They get weaponized. Then they act, at machine speed, and you may never know it happened until it's too late.
- No breach required. An agent that was never attacked can still misread its instructions and act with complete confidence on a wrong conclusion.
- Today's security and governance layers check prompts, policies or outputs. They don't control the sequence of actions an agent actually takes before it takes them.
- SMEs feel this most: they are adopting AI fast, but often without a dedicated AI security team or enterprise-grade protection.
- Unsafe agent actions can cause harm in payments, software development, personnel data handling, legal operations and health administration, and can trigger unintended regulatory breaches, before a human can step in.

## How it works

1. Learn: builds each agent's behavioural fingerprint from its normal action sequences.
2. Check: scores each next action before it runs.
3. Detect: spots sequence deviations in real time.
4. Decide: allows, pauses for review, or blocks the action.
5. Prove: every block is signed (Ed25519) and anyone can verify it.

Example: a payments agent normally runs read_file → match_ledger → write_report. When it attempts an http.post to an account never seen for this agent, the sequence is not in its baseline. Agentic Guardians blocks the action before it runs and issues a signed Detection Certificate.

## Why it is different

- Not AI watching AI. AI guarding AI puts the lock and the thief in the same paradigm: a prompt that reaches the agent can reach the guard. You cannot ask a corrupted process to report its own corruption.
- Agentic Guardians works outside the language layer. It reads actions and never reads prompts, so it can't be injected and it can't be persuaded.
- Prompt filters and guardrails inspect language and share the model's attack surface. Logs and monitoring find problems after the fact. Manual review can't keep up with machine speed. Agentic Guardians acts before execution.
- Lightweight enough for SMEs, robust enough for regulated workflows.
- Built on peer-reviewed research into behavioural sequence models (IEEE Access, 2020), applied in production fraud detection before being pointed at AI agents.

## Why now

- Everyone wants agents. Almost nobody trusts them yet. That gap is where Agentic Guardians lives.
- The industry answered "how do I build this agent?" Nobody answered "how do I make sure it's safe?"
- As companies hand work to agents, they remove the people who would have caught a rogue one. Agentic Guardians is the oversight layer that's left.
- AI agents can trigger unintended breaches of GDPR, the EU AI Act and other rules. Organisations need runtime trust infrastructure that supports auditable AI deployment.
